p1: THIS PANEL: Mongle is shy — its body squashed down a little smaller and lower on its stool, eyes glancing down, a tiny round 'o' mouth as if whispering very quietly toward the back, a faint blush. The four side-dish plates are still EMPTY. The friend still looks down at the grill, turning the pork belly with the tongs. The imo still has her BACK to the camera at the back counter, wiping it — she does not notice anything.
p2: THIS PANEL: Mongle stretches its whole body TALL and leans toward the back of the restaurant, eyes squeezed shut, mouth wide open — shouting as loud as it can toward the imo. The friend looks at Mongle, surprised, tongs paused in the air above the grill. The imo still has her BACK to the camera at the back counter. The four side-dish plates are still EMPTY.
p3: THIS PANEL: the friend lifts one hand high in a casual, confident wave toward the back counter, smiling with her mouth open as if calling out cheerfully; her other hand still holds the tongs. Mongle (normal size again) turns to look up at the friend, curious. At the back counter the imo has already TURNED AROUND to face the camera, smiling brightly and lifting a small stack of white side-dish bowls. The four plates on our table are still EMPTY.
p4: THIS PANEL: Mongle is SHOCKED — eyes very wide, a big round open mouth, its body leaning toward the friend. The friend smiles at Mongle. In the MIDDLE of the image, on the open wooden floor, the imo is WALKING toward our table carrying a felt tray with small bowls full of red kimchi, bean sprouts and fresh lettuce — about halfway between the counter and our table, facing the camera. The four plates on our table are still EMPTY.
p5: THIS PANEL: the imo now stands right beside our table at the RIGHT BACK edge of the table (behind and a little to the left of the friend, between about 48% and 70% of the image width), smiling, setting refilled side dishes onto the table — the four small plates are now FULL again (red kimchi, bean sprouts, seasoned spinach, and the lettuce basket full of fresh green lettuce). The friend laughs warmly, one hand waving side to side in a friendly 'no, no' gesture toward Mongle. Mongle tilts its body sideways, confused, eyes looking up at the imo.
p6: THIS PANEL: the side dishes on our table are FULL (red kimchi, bean sprouts, seasoned spinach, lettuce). The imo is back at the back counter with her BACK to the camera. Mongle takes a huge deep breath — its whole body INFLATED round like a balloon, cheeks puffed, eyes determined and shining, looking toward the back. The friend watches Mongle, amused, chin on her hand.
p7: THIS PANEL: Mongle stretches SUPER TALL toward the back of the restaurant, eyes squeezed shut, mouth WIDE open — shouting happily with all its might. The friend laughs and covers both ears with her hands. At the back counter the imo has turned around to face us, delighted, one hand on her cheek. The side dishes on our table are FULL.
p8: THIS PANEL — the big finale: in the CENTRE of our table, beside the grill, stands a TALL wobbly TOWER of stacked small side-dish bowls — eight or nine different felt banchan stacked high (red kimchi, bean sprouts, spinach, fish cake, japchae noodles, yellow pickled radish, black beans, cucumber, potato), the tower rising up to about 45% of the image height. Next to it a black stone pot (ttukbaegi) of fluffy golden steamed egg (gyeranjjim) puffed high above the rim, a little steam rising. The imo stands right beside our table at the right back edge (between about 48% and 70% of the image width), placing one more small bowl on top of the tower and winking. Mongle bounces up on its stool, eyes sparkling, blushing, a huge happy open smile. The friend's jaw drops in amazement, both hands on her cheeks.
